solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Engine inlets for gas producers

parts.note: a motor is an engine
mouths are openings or inlets, as of a river or harbour

explanation.surface: A technical description of the air intakes on engines that produce gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' here is idle chatter, not fuel or vapour.
explanation.definitionFit: To gas is to chatter at length, so people who never stop talking are producers of gas.

clue.text: Blokes with ring — that's improving

parts.note: blokes is British slang for men
a ding is the ringing sound of a bell

explanation.surface: Men wearing a ring are getting better, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Mending means recovering health or getting better, as in 'on the mend'.

clue.text: Ibert composed for some people

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so the letters of the composer's name are reordered

explanation.surface: The French composer Jacques Ibert wrote music for a select few.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' looks like a nod to the composer Ibert, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribe is a group of people sharing ancestry or culture.

clue.text: Managed most of royal household in enmity

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, so ran means managed

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter

parts.note: the court is a monarch's household and retinue

explanation.surface: Running the royal household brought bitter feuding.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep-seated bitterness or hostility, a synonym of enmity.

clue.text: Painting skilfully, one might gush

parts.note: an oil is a painting done in oils
well means skilfully or competently

explanation.surface: An art critic gushes over a deftly done canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gush' suggests effusive praise for the painting; it is a literal gusher of crude.
explanation.definitionFit: A drilled shaft that strikes crude can spout petroleum in a gusher.

clue.text: Nothing comes up after article speculates …

indicators.note: after signals that the nothing-and-rising part follows the article

parts.note: the is the definite article
O, the round figure zero, means nothing
rises means comes up, as the sun does

explanation.surface: A columnist wonders aloud when nothing appears after the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To theorise is to form hypotheses, which is to speculate.

clue.text: … surprise celebrity story — article's dropped

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

indicators.note: dropped means the article is left out of the word for story

parts.note: a tale is a story
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A shock: a celebrity tale has been cut from the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle someone is to give them a sudden surprise or fright.

clue.text: Web being rejected by Welshman creates strain

indicators.note: something rejected is turned back, so the word for web is read backwards

parts.note: a net is a web or mesh
Sion is a Welsh form of the man's name John

explanation.surface: A Welshman turning down a spider's web or the internet causes stress.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension and strain are synonyms for stress, whether mental or physical tautness.

clue.text: Isn't he first off in economy?

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about whether a man leads the way when it comes to saving money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like part of 'first off' but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Thriftiness is careful use of money and resources, which is economy.

clue.text: Drag fish westwards, in wind's direction

indicators.note: in an across entry, going west means reading right to left, so these words are written backwards

parts.note: to draw is to drag or pull
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: An angler hauls a catch west, downwind.
explanation.definitionFit: The leeward side is the one the wind blows towards, i.e. downwind, the direction the wind travels.

clue.text: Take apart second answer in disguise

indicators.note: in means the two letters are placed inside the word for disguise

parts.note: to dissemble is to disguise one's true feelings

explanation.surface: Pulling apart the second answer to see what it really hides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' needs the second-and-answer pair placed after the first two letters of the disguise word, not in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To disassemble a machine is to dismantle or take it to pieces.

clue.text: Pay hike is secured by overturning hearing

indicators.note: something secured by another is held within it, so the first word goes inside
overturning flips the word for hearing so it reads backwards

parts.note: an ear is a sense of hearing, as in 'have an ear for music'

explanation.surface: A salary increase is guaranteed by overturning a verdict at a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' suggests a court case, but it is the sense of hearing, the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A raise is the American and informal term for a salary increase.

clue.text: Thinks too much of bowlers' statistics

definitions.meaning: to value something more highly than it deserves
in cricket an over is six balls bowled, and an over rate measures how many overs a fielding side bowls per hour

explanation.surface: A cricket fan is too impressed by the bowling figures.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's over rate is the number of overs bowled per hour; the second reading splits the answer into OVER RATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who overvalues a thing esteems it beyond its worth, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Travel back in grief, upset and more gloomy?

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
something upset is knocked over and jumbled, so the letters of grief are rearranged
going back reverses the word for travel

parts.note: to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Revisiting a sorrow leaves one upset and sadder.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that gloom is taken literally as murky weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Foggier weather is murkier and darker, a literal kind of gloom.

clue.text: Short-sighted minx with band in charge of sandwiches put on

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child, like a minx

indicators.note: to sandwich is to hold between two layers, so the band and in-charge letters enclose the word for put on

parts.note: O is a ring shape, a band
IC is the abbreviation for in charge
a light that is put on is lit

explanation.surface: A short-sighted girl leading a band handles lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short-sighted' looks like poor eyesight but means lacking foresight.
explanation.definitionFit: An impolitic act is unwise, showing a lack of foresight about consequences.

clue.text: Reduced payments, discounting fine for tenants

parts.note: less means reduced or lower

indicators.note: discounting means leaving out, so the letter for fine is removed

parts.note: fees are payments for services
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: Lower charges, before any penalty, for people renting.
explanation.definitionFit: Lessees hold a property under a lease, which makes them tenants of the landlord.

clue.text: Thoroughly awkward about daughter and husband

indicators.note: the word for awkward goes about, i.e. around, the daughter's letter

parts.note: inept means clumsy or awkward
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A clumsy family member fusses over a daughter and husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Something examined in depth is studied comprehensively, which is to say thoroughly.

clue.text: Party getting good's over — that's annoying!

parts.note: a do is a party
G is the abbreviation for good
gone means over or finished

explanation.surface: The fun party has ended: what a shame!
explanation.definitionFit: Doggone is an American euphemism for damned, an exclamation of irritation.

clue.text: Henry adopts fund, exchanging halves to make a small number

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so Henry's short form holds the other part

parts.note: Hal is a pet form of Henry, as Shakespeare's Prince Hal

indicators.note: the first two and last two letters of the word fund change places

explanation.surface: Henry takes on a fund and swaps its two parts around to make a little money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a small number' is not a figure but a few people or things.
explanation.definitionFit: A handful is as many as a hand can hold, so only a few.

clue.text: Sorcerer involves idiot in manipulation

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up or contain, so the sorcerer's word holds the idiot's

parts.note: a mage is a magician or sorcerer
an ass is a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: A wizard drags a fool into some trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manipulation' suggests trickery to match the sorcerer, but it means kneading muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: Massage is the kneading and rubbing of muscles by hand, a physical kind of manipulation.

clue.text: Model Eva is M&S great

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A fashion model named Eva is the star face of Marks & Spencer, a British high-street chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a noun describing Eva, but it is the anagram signal; M&S gives the letters M and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Massive means huge or great in size.

clue.text: Gold to recover value, according to what's heard

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to rally is to recover, as prices do after a fall

explanation.surface: Gold prices are rising again, so the market report says.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurally means by ear or by listening.

clue.text: Spur factories to produce purple fruits

parts.note: to egg on is to spur or urge
plants are industrial factories

explanation.surface: Urging industrial sites to grow crops of plums.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubergines, known in America as eggplants, are glossy purple fruits used as vegetables.

clue.text: Beat the never-ending cheat

indicators.note: with no ending, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to rob is to cheat or swindle someone

explanation.surface: Defeat the swindler who never stops.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a pulse or rhythmic beat, as of the heart.

clue.text: Male and female in race crime

indicators.note: in means these letters are placed inside the race's letters

parts.note: TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle race
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man and a woman are caught up in a race to commit a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft, stealing property, is a crime.

clue.text: Lacking O?

definitions.meaning: without enough of something, deficient in it
the letter O, as in o'clock, is a shortened form of the word of

explanation.surface: A one-word puzzle asking what is missing from the letter O.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: O is SHORT for OF, as in o'clock or will-o'-the-wisp.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short of something means having too little of it, i.e. lacking it.

clue.text: Occasionally, finches followed maritime feature

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so every other letter is taken from these words

explanation.surface: Now and then, small birds came after something at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet of floating frozen sea water is a common sight in polar seas.

clue.text: Remarkably, VIP swaps starter of carpaccio for centre part of cutlet

indicators.note: swaps here means one letter is exchanged for another within the VIP's title

parts.note: Excellency is the formal title of an ambassador or governor, a VIP

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter
the centre part of the word is its two middle letters

explanation.surface: A dignitary at dinner swaps a starter of raw beef for a slice of the main course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter of carpaccio' is C and 'centre part of cutlet' is TL; the final C of EXCELLENCY becomes TL.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something excellently means doing it outstandingly well, which is to say remarkably.
